title: Homological Thresholds in Randomly Monitored Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
authors: Yoshito Watanabe, Daiki Sasamoto, Bo Han, Simon Trebst
abstract: Random projective measurements are an effective tool to model the interlinked phenomenology of monitoring, inferring, and decoding highly entangled states such as quantum error-correcting codes. At the same time, the study of such monitored dynamics has opened a new arena for critical phenomena, renewing longstanding questions in disordered statistical mechanics, including percolation, random-bond models, and Nishimori physics. Here we investigate the robustness of stabilizer quantum error-correcting codes under a single round of independently sampled single-qubit Pauli measurements and demonstrate that their threshold behavior falls into two broad categories - geometric and homological percolation transitions, with the toric code and color code being the principal examples for each class. We establish the distinct character of these two threshold theories by analyzing the logical-support criteria of these codes and by providing numerical estimates of their respective critical exponents obtained from optimized stabilizer simulations of large-scale systems with over one million qubits. Our framework extends to non-CSS, subsystem, higher-dimensional, and Floquet stabilizer codes and allows us to determine their respective threshold phase diagrams. We exemplify how the latter provide quantitative and qualitative guidance for the computationally more demanding problems of tunable learning and maximum-likelihood decoding. As a practical application of our framework, we discuss the robustness of the gross code.
summary: This work analyzes how quantum error-correcting codes fail when subjected to random monitoring measurements. It establishes that the failure mechanism can be classified into two distinct types of percolation transitions: geometric and homological. This provides a powerful, unified theoretical framework for understanding the robustness of topological quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper investigates the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes when subjected to random single-qubit Pauli measurements, mapping this process to critical phenomena.
main_result: The threshold behavior for code failure falls into two distinct categories: geometric and homological percolation transitions, exemplified by the toric and color codes, respectively.
method: The analysis uses algebraic and homological methods, mapping logical information loss to the criteria for noncontractible loops, and employs numerical simulations to determine critical exponents.
model_or_system: The system studied is stabilizer quantum error-correcting codes (e.g., toric code, color code) defined on lattices, whose stability is tested by random Pauli measurements.
key_observables: Threshold probability for logical subspace collapse, critical exponents, and the logical-support criteria.
important_parameters: Measurement probabilities ($p_X, p_Y, p_Z$), lattice structure (square vs. honeycomb), and system size (up to one million qubits).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the monitoring process to logical support criteria, and phase diagrams are based on analytically obtained pure-axis thresholds.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate tunable-learning and random-measurement phase diagrams for the toric and color codes, showing logical survival versus collapse regimes, and depict the algebraic structure of logical operators.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the failure mechanisms of different codes under measurement, distinguishing between geometric and homological failure modes, and extends the framework to various code types.
why_interesting: It connects the abstract concepts of topological order and quantum error correction thresholds directly to well-established concepts in statistical mechanics, such as percolation theory and critical phenomena.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Tunable-learning and random-measurement phase diagrams. (a) Toric-code tunable-learning phase diagram of Ref. [13], parameterized by the measurement strengths (γX, γY , γZ). The cyan boundary marks the Nishimori learning transition. (b,c) Semi-analytic phase diagrams for the random Pauli-measurement protocol studied here, for (b) the toric code and (c) the color code. The phase boundaries separate regimes in which encoded logical information survives from those in which it is collapsed by the measurements. The measurement probabilities are parameterized as pX = r sin2 θ sin2 ϕ, pY = r cos2 θ, and pZ = r sin2 θ cos2 ϕ, with r = pX +pY +pZ. The boundaries are approximate constructions...

FIG. 2. Local structure of logical operators. (a,b) Square-lattice toric code and honeycomb-lattice (6, 6, 6) color code, with repre- sentative noncontractible logical Z operators. Red and blue sym- bols denote X- and Z-type stabilizers, respectively. (c,d) Multipli- cation by local Z stabilizers deforms these representatives without changing their logical action. Toric-code deformations preserve an unbranched-loop description, whereas color-code strings can split and recombine at three-string junctions, producing branched colored- string representations. This contrast underlies ordinary geometric connectivity in the toric code and non-geometric homological con- nectivity in the color code.

FIG. 4. Y -assisted logical Z measurement in the toric code. (a) Blue and green markers denote qubits measured in the Z and Y bases, respectively. Up to an irrelevant phase, the product of the cor- responding measured Pauli operators is AvBp1Bp2LZ, thereby im- plementing a logical Z measurement, even though the Z-measured edges alone support no noncontractible Z loop. (b) Schematic pX = 0 section of the logical-survival phase diagram. The blue sliver de- notes the additional logical-Z-measurement regime produced coop- eratively by Y and Z measurements below the Z-only percolation threshold pZ = 1/2, marked by the blue line. Its width is exagger- ated for visibility.

FIG. 3. Numerical logical-survival phase diagrams. Phase bound- aries for (a) the toric code and (b) the color code are shown in the positive octant. Red wireframes show the semi-analytic construction from the pure-axis thresholds, while colored symbols show numer- ical boundary estimates obtained from finite-size scaling of the co- herent information. Crosses mark estimates compatible with rc = 1 within uncertainty; the corresponding thermodynamic critical radii may lie slightly below unity (see text). (c) Representative planar cuts. (d) The fitted scaling exponent ν along the same cuts as a func- tion of the in-plane angle α, oriented as indicated in (a,b).

FIG. 5. Geometric versus homological connectivity in the color code. Z-measured qubits are shown in blue. (a) The two measured qubits directly connect the same-color plaquettes u and v, giving the direct link u ∼v. (b) The direct links u ∼w and w ∼v con- nect u and v through an ordinary geometric path on the same-color triangular sublattice. (c) No direct link is present among u, v, and w. Nevertheless, multiplying the measured Pauli product by the two outlined plaquette stabilizers BsBw deforms its support into the di- rect connection shown in (a). Thus u and v are homologically but not geometrically connected.
